cloze.title: 原文选词填空
cloze.instruction: 从词库中选择合适的词填入空白，每词使用一次，保留原文词形。大小写不影响判分。

parts.text: In this series we go behind the scenes to reveal the ingenious tricks and innovations that have transformed

production over the course of a century.

Snakes in my mac and cheese

Today, one of the most celebrated sound designers in cinema is Ben Burtt. For Raiders of the Lost Ark (1981), he created the sound of snakes

across the floor of the Egyptian tomb by running his fingers through a dish of macaroni and cheese.

Burtt also created what is possibly the most famous sound effect in the history of cinema: the light sabre swoosh. For this, he used a

microphone to record the hum of a film projector being played through speakers. He waved the microphone in front of the speakers, imitating the characters on screen.

This created a combination of

effects, including a doppler shift (the change in pitch when the source of a sound is moving), along with swells and fades in volume as the microphone passed each speaker.

Foley also steers where we look onscreen, and how we feel. A close

of fabric during a tense scene can pull us inside a character’s head, as we hear what they’re hearing.

The sound team behind The Lord of the Rings trilogy, led by David Farmer, Ethan Van der Ryn and Mike Hopkins, became known for their
Foley methods. They built the enormous audible world of Middle Earth from scratch – every sword shing, armour-plated boot, chainmail clink and bridle

.

They also spent many late nights recording real bow and arrow draw, release and impact sounds at a nearby graveyard for realism.

This effort in sound acquisition creates a massive job for sound editors after the fact. Hundreds of recordings need to be sorted,

and synced into a mix.

In praise of Foley

Despite these examples, Foley recorded specifically for a film or television show is rare.

This type of bespoke sound work takes money, time, hundreds of

, and a skilled team. A typical independent production, meanwhile, will have one sound designer (maybe two) and a deadline.

With such limited resources, it’s often not viable to record organic sound, such as for footsteps, on
. Location audio is often noisy and uncontrolled – not to mention the picture edit isn’t locked in yet.
